Abhishek Agarwal: 
Hi, good afternoon everyone, and welcome to Purple Style Labs' Pernia's Pop-Up Shop Q1 FY27 
Earnings Conference Call. Along with me, we have the SGA team, our Investor Relations 
Advisors. It is a pleasure for us to address analysts and our investors as a listed company for the 
first time. I hope all of you have gone through the investor presentation that we have uploaded 
on the exchanges and also on our company's website. 
 
Before I take you through our financial performance, I would like to spend some time explaining 
our business and how we have evolved it over the last few years, as we believe that 
understanding the underlying business model is important to interpret our financial performance 
better. 
 
Our core business, Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, is one of the largest and fastest-growing multi-brand 
luxury omni-channel fashion platforms in India, serving customers across India and international 
markets. We offer a carefully curated selection of luxury fashion sourced from more than 1,100 
active designer brands and 2 lakh plus SKUs designer products on our website. 
 
Our product portfolio spans women's wear, men's wear, jewellery, accessories, and kids wear, 
with a strong focus on the occasion wear segment. We combine online discovery with large-
format experience centers, allowing customers to explore a wide range of designers on our 
website while providing personalized styling and an immersive shopping experience at our 
stores. Therefore, we see online and offline not as competing channels, but as complementary 
in our customer journey. 
 
Another important aspect of our business model is our inventory strategy. We follow a breadth 
over depth approach, offering a wide range of designs while maintaining mostly singular 
quantity of individual products at our stores. Depending on the product category, we use a 
combination of outright purchase, backorder, and consignment models with different 
commercial terms and varying markdowns across designer brands. 
 
The unique aspect of our business model is the backorder model, in which the customer places 
the order first with upfront payment, following which we procure the product from designer with 
a delivery window of 7 to 90 days depending on the product. This approach allows us to maintain

a very wide curation with efficient inventory management, while limiting the need to carry large 
quantities of individual designer products at our stores. 
 
PSL had acquired Pernia's Pop-Up Shop in February 2018, prior to which it was primarily an e-
commerce platform. Post the acquisition, our journey can broadly be understood through three 
distinct generations. You can refer to the slide seven on our presentation for the same. 
 
Post the acquisition, our journey can broadly be understood through these three generations. The 
first generation from FY19 to '21 was all about laying the foundation. During this period, we 
transformed Pernia's Pop-Up Shop into an omni-channel platform, opened eight experience 
centers across 5 cities, including London, and built the designer brand supply across all 
categories and price points. This foundation helped us grow the platform GMV from INR23 
crores in FY19 to INR66 crores in FY21. 
 
Now, the second generation from FY22 to '24 was about scaling the footprint. We scaled our 
experience centers' presence to 13 locations across 8 cities and started the transition towards 
large-format experience centers, which typically ranged between 20,000 to 60,000 square feet, 
and deepened our designer supply, particularly in women's wear of 1 lakh plus and men's wear 
segment. During this period, the GMV increased almost 10x to INR622 crores in FY24 versus 
FY21, while AOV almost doubled from INR22,000 in FY21 to INR46,000 in FY24. 
 
Now, FY24 we then consciously trimmed the long tail of both designers and customers and 
sharpened our focus on luxury. This marked the beginning of what we call as the third generation 
of growth. Starting in FY25 with a focus on optimizing the platform first. Then after March '25, 
we have actively changed growth gears and opened four large experience centers during FY26. 
 
The iconic Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi locations have been fully operational since Q2 of 
FY26. Then another important project, our Linking Road, Bandra, Mumbai store opened towards 
the end of March '26, alongside opened one of the most important milestones of our recent 
journey, a flagship store on Madison Avenue, Manhattan, New York. 
 
During this time, the average order value increased from INR46,000 in FY24 to INR76,000 in 
FY26, and in the first quarter of '27 has jumped to a further INR86,000. FY27 is therefore the 
first full year with which we have started realizing the growth trajectory of the investment that 
we had made in the last financial year. 
 
Now, please refer to the Slide 9 on our presentation to understand our geographical expansion 
strategy. This evolution across three generation reflects in how we have scaled our presence in 
the relevant markets of our industry. In the first generation, we focused on establishing our initial 
footprint across key cities through eight small stores, laying the base for future growth. We also 
established our first international presence in London in the same window. 
 
Now, in the second generation, we scaled this footprint and began moving from bigger stores, 
starting in our largest market, Delhi, which has a strong concentration of affluent customers and

where we see a stronger spending potential by adding four large experience centers in Mumbai,

INR205 crores and Delhi at INR166 crores, which together contributing more than 50% of our 
total GMV, while international markets also remain key contributor to our platform. 
 
So, just to summarize the geographical growth strategy, in the first generation, our focus was 
establishing physical touch points and building the initial omni-channel ecosystem. As we 
moved to the second generation, we developed a deeper understanding of the luxury customer 
base and the importance of physical shopping environment. This led us to transition towards 
large-format experience centers, typically ranging from 20,000 to 60,000 square feet, opening 
our first large-format store in Mehrauli, Delhi. 
 
In the third generation, these large-format stores have become integral part of our platform 
strategy and with the focus shifting from simply expanding our physical footprint to improving 
the customer economics. These large stores act as a discovery and ordering platform where 
customers can explore a much broader assortment with backorder capabilities, receive 
personalized styling, and wherever required, also access our wider digital catalog as well, while 
their presence at the store. 
 
This is reflected in the steady increase of our average order value from INR27,000 in FY ‘19 to 
INR46,000 in FY ‘24 to INR76,000 in FY ‘26, and eventually INR86,000 in the last Q1 FY ‘27. 
While our annual GMV increased from INR23 crores in FY ‘19 to INR722 crores in FY ‘26. 
 
Post March ‘24, we entered the third generation of our growth with strategy of trimming the 
long tail. During FY ‘25, we actively reduced the number of designers on the website and scaled 
down the marketing spend to trim away the low-ticket size transaction of our platform. So, if 
you move to Slide 12 to understand the trimming of the long tail of customers, so historically 
the focus was always on acquiring more customers and building the scale. 
 
Since the implementation, the value contribution of our customer base had increased 
significantly. Average GMV per customer grew sharply to INR67,000 in FY ‘24, which

INR406 crores in FY ‘26. Similarly, in FY ‘22, our Top 50,000 customers contributed INR234

INR46,000 by FY ‘24. And in the third generation, as we built the focus on luxury positioning 
and higher-value customers, this further increased to INR76,000 in FY ‘26. 
 
Now, let's try to understand our supply side. The designer brands ecosystem which has also gone 
through a significant transformation as part of the trimming the long tail strategy. In the first and 
second generation, our priority was to build a very large universe of brands on our platform 
across price point and categories. However, as the platform scaled, we realized that a very long 
tail increases the complexity across merchandising, inventory management, designer 
relationships, and execution. 
 
In FY ‘24, the Top 100 designers were contributing 67% of the sales on the platform. Therefore, 
since FY ‘25, we have consciously moved to a more curated designer universe, focusing our 
resources on brands and with stronger customer recognition, established product market fit, and 
the potential to scale. 
 
As a result, we have reduced our active designer base from 1,910 brands in FY ‘24 to 1,109 
brands in FY ‘26, while the AOV increased from INR46,000 to INR76,000 in the same period. 
Importantly, we continue to maintain a significant breadth of products on our website while 
reducing the operational intensity that comes associated with the long tail.

category mix. In the first generation, the objective was to establish a wide supply of products 
from all designer categories. In the second generation, we began building greater depth in luxury 
women's wear, which is 1 lakh plus price point, and men's wear. Because of this change in 
strategy, the 1 lakh plus women's wear increased from INR7 crores in FY ‘21 to INR187 crores 
in FY ‘24, while men's wear grew from just INR2 crores in FY ‘21 to INR96 crores in FY ‘24. 
 
Now, in the third generation, we are sharpening the focus towards higher-value categories, which 
has led the 1 lakh plus women's wear generating INR312 crores GMV in FY ‘26 compared to 
INR187 crores in FY ‘24. Men's wear has also grown meaningfully to INR132 crores in FY ‘26. 
At the same time, the lower value below 35,000 women's wear has declined from INR162 crores
